dial.summary: Six of eight macro indicators are supportive as the BTC Accumulation thesis firms: ISM Manufacturing holds at a four-year high of 55.6%, the 2s10s yield curve steepened to +0.42% on a 30-day basis, stablecoin dominance compressed further to 12.6% as capital rotates into risk assets, and DXY holds neutral at 99.97 just below the 100 headwind boundary; BTC.D firm at 56.5% with TOTAL crypto rising to $2.27T and BTC at $63,943, while the key risks are elevated real yields (2.47%, headwind) and July NFP Friday (consensus ~85k vs June's 57k) and CPI Aug 12 as the next regime-change catalysts ahead of the September 15–16 FOMC.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $102,663.81B (~$102.7T) for June 2026; July global aggregate not yet published (central banks report M2 with ~30-day lag); US M2 weekly continued rising through late July—$23.3T for the week of July 6 (H.6 released July 28), up from $23.16T June monthly record high, 28th consecutive monthly increase, +5.6% YoY; 4-week trend up (US M2 weekly +$0.14T vs June monthly, global aggregate uptrend intact, YoY growth rate stable at ~5-6%); status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY contracting headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released August 3, 2026 at 55.6%—2.3pp above June's 53.3%, beat 54.0% estimate, highest since May 2022 and seventh consecutive expansion month; all five sub-indexes in expansion: Production 58.5% (+6.3pts, best since Nov 2021), Employment 52.8% (first expansion in 33 months), New Orders 56.7% (seventh consecutive expansion), Backlogs 55.0%, Prices 71.1% (still elevated, -1.9pts); S&P Global US Composite PMI also rose to 53.6 in July from 51.9 in June (8-month high), driven by services accelerating; ISM Services PMI for July scheduled Aug 5 at 10:00 AM ET with prior June reading 54.0%; 4-week trend up: 53.3% (June) → 55.6% (July) = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 AND rising; headwind threshold of 62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.97 on August 4, 2026 (close), down from 101.34 on July 1; dollar fell to intraday low ~99.8 at start of August amid fresh yen strength and partial foreign investor pivot out of dollar positions before recovering; 30-day trend: ~101.34 (July 1) → 99.97 (Aug 4) = -1.37%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold, trend remains down; status NEUTRAL per ICE DXY spot threshold (at 99.97, just below the 100 headwind boundary and above the 97.5 supportive boundary); July NFP (Aug 7, consensus ~85k) and CPI (Aug 12) are next directional catalysts—a weak NFP could push DXY below 97.5 (flipping to supportive), a strong print could restore above 100 (headwind).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield) at 2.47% as of July 31, 2026 (FRED H.15); 10-year TIPS auction on July 23 cleared at a real yield of 2.438%, confirming the level; nominal 10Y declined from 4.75% (July 31) to 4.63% (Aug 4) while 2Y fell from 4.28% to 4.21%, suggesting real yields may have eased marginally in early August from the July 31 peak; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (July 2) → 2.47% (July 31) = +29bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold AND rising on 4-week basis; September FOMC cut expectations remain modest after ISM Manufacturing beat at 55.6%; July CPI on Aug 12 is the primary real-yield compression catalyst).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 4, 2026: DGS10 4.63%, DGS2 4.21%, spread = +0.42% (+42bps); July 31 spread was +0.47% (10Y 4.75%, 2Y 4.28%)—both yields fell roughly in parallel as Q2 GDP (+1.5% vs 2.1% est) and soft labor conditions weighed; 4-week comparison: July 2 spread ~+0.35% → Aug 4 +0.42% = steepening of +7bps, above the 5bps flat threshold, trend up; status supportive (positive AND steepening on 30-day basis confirmed; headwind threshold of < -50bps not applicable at current +42bps spread; FOMC minutes Aug 19 and September 15–16 meeting are next major curve catalysts).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL from H.4.1 released July 30, 2026: $6,738,190M ($6.738T) for week ending July 29, 2026—down ~$9B from the prior week (July 22: ~$6.747T); next H.4.1 release August 6, 2026; Fed assets remain ~$95B higher than one year ago; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.72T (early July) → $6.738T (July 29) = +$0.018T (+0.27%), within the <0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (flat to marginally stable; QT effectively paused since mid-2025; no aggressive runoff with rising overnight rates; balance sheet holding at post-2022 plateau).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: Live funding rate data inaccessible—CoinGlass returned HTTP 403; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h; contextual signals: BTC at $63,943 on August 5, 2026 (+0.98% on day), market cap $1.28T, circulating supply 20.07M BTC, total crypto $2.27T (+0.7% on day), BTC dominance 56.5% (up from 56.42% on Aug 4); S&P Global composite PMI 53.6 in July (8-month high) and ISM Manufacturing 55.6% (4-year high) confirm macro expansion consistent with spot accumulation rather than leveraged speculation; funding remains well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June); status supportive (near-zero positive rate signals healthy long bias without overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $286.9B as of August 2, 2026 (stablecoin.com: USDT $183.3B, USDC $72.0B, combined 89.0% share); total crypto market cap $2.27T (August 5, 2026); stablecoin dominance $286.9B / $2.27T ≈ 12.6%; 30-day trend down: June 30 ~$305B / $2.10T = ~14.5% → Aug 2 ~12.6%, compression of ~1.9pp as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets over the past 30+ days; status supportive (falling on 30-day basis; headwind threshold requires rising dominance WHILE TOTAL crypto is also rising—not met since dominance fell while TOTAL rose from $2.10T to $2.27T on 30-day basis).

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 1, 2026)
upcoming.note: Weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET—labor market pulse one day ahead of July NFP (August 7); prior week ended July 26: ~226k; also the date of the Fed's H.4.1 balance sheet release (data for week ending July 30, 2026, providing first post-July-29 balance sheet read); a print above 250k would add September rate cut pricing and could compress real yields from 2.47%; a sub-220k print would reinforce the strong ISM Manufacturing signal (55.6%) and add upward pressure to yields and DXY, which is holding at 99.97 just below the 100 headwind threshold; consensus expects a steady 225–235k range given moderately softening labor conditions.

upcoming.title: Employment Situation / NFP (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings; consensus: ~80–88k payrolls (vs June's soft 57k), unemployment rate steady at 4.2–4.3%; primary labor market read ahead of the September 15–16 FOMC; macro backdrop: DXY 99.97 (neutral), real yields 2.47% (headwind), 2s10s +0.42% (supportive), ISM Manufacturing 55.6% (supportive); a weak NFP (<75k) would push September cut odds above 80% and could compress real yields toward 2% and DXY below 97.5 (flipping to supportive); a strong beat (>150k) would reinforce the ISM Manufacturing surge and may push DXY above 100 (restoring headwind status); June's 57k was well below consensus, making a July rebound to 85–100k likely but uncertain.

upcoming.title: CPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the most important inflation print ahead of the September 15–16 FOMC; arrives five days after July NFP (August 7); real yields at 2.47% and DXY at 99.97 make a soft CPI the primary catalyst for real yield compression and a potential DXY break below 97.5 (which would flip DXY status to supportive); a hot print risks pushing DXY back above 100 (restoring headwind status) and is the principal risk to the BTC Accumulation thesis; core PCE came in soft at 0.1% MoM in June, suggesting disinflation may be resuming; however, ISM Manufacturing Prices remained elevated at 71.1% in July, signaling pipeline cost pressures that could keep CPI sticky above 3%.
